fi-osphronemus-goramy.title: Giant Gourami
fi-osphronemus-goramy.summary: The giant gourami, Osphronemus goramy, is a large gourami from Borneo, Java, Sumatra, Thailand, Indo-china and the Malay Peninsula. Reaching 70 cm and living for over 20 years, it is often sold as a…
rows: Borneo , Java , Sumatra , Thailand , Indo-china and the Malay Peninsula.
notes: Provide hiding places in the form of robust large rocks and bogwood .
Floating plants are preferable though these may be eaten.

fi-trichogaster-lalius.title: Dwarf Gourami
fi-trichogaster-lalius.summary: The dwarf gourami, Trichogaster lalius, is a labyrinth fish from Pakistan, northern India and Bangladesh. All the fish in the trade are mass-produced, and several line-bred colour forms are sold,…
rows: Omnivore. Thought to be omnivorous in nature, feeding on small invertebrates, algae and other aufwuchs .
Widely distributed through Pakistan , northern India and Bangladesh .
notes: Like most Anabantoids, dwarf gouramis do not appreciate fast-moving or turbulent water.
Try to keep flow to a minimum in any set-up containing them.

fi-trichogaster-trichopterus.title: Three-spot Gourami
fi-trichogaster-trichopterus.summary: The three-spot gourami, Trichopodus trichopterus, is a labyrinth fish found mostly in the Mekong basin of Southeast Asia and southern China. The natural form is blue-grey with three spots, but gold,…
rows: Omnivore. Wild fish are fairly generalised omnivores , munching on both terrestrial and aquatic plants as well as algae , small invertebrates, other items of zooplankton and detritus .
Occurs mostly in the River Mekong basin in southern China, Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Thailand, Myanmar and Malaysia .
notes: A planted aquarium with some floating cover and open areas for swimming suits this species.

fi-macropodus-opercularis.title: Macropodus opercularis
fi-macropodus-opercularis.summary: The paradise fish, Macropodus opercularis, is a labyrinth fish from China south of the Yangtze, including Taiwan and Hainan, plus Vietnam and Laos. Imported to France in 1869, it was among the very…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Omnivore. Likely to prey on insect larvae and suchlike in nature, and should be offered small live or frozen Daphnia , Artemia , white worm , grindal worm , etc., in captivity.
Occurs naturally in China, south of the Yangtze ( Chang Jiang ) River system, including Taiwan and Hainan Island, northern and central Vietnam, and northeastern Laos.
notes: Can be maintained in a fully-decorated aquarium although many breeders prefer not to use a substrate for ease of maintenance.

Driftwood roots and branches can be used and placed such a way that a few shady spots are formed, while some floating or surface vegetation should be included if the aim is to breed the fish (see 'Reproduction').

fi-colisa-chuna.title: Red Honey Gourami
fi-colisa-chuna.summary: The honey gourami, Trichogaster chuna, is a labyrinth fish from the Ganges and Brahmaputra systems of India and Bangladesh, with records from Nepal. Virtually all fish on sale are commercially…
rows: Aggressive / best alone or carefully chosen tankmates

schooling fishes it does seem to require interaction with conspecifics and displays more interesting behaviour when maintained in numbers, meaning the purchase of no less than 4-6 specimens is recommended.
Herbivore / algae browser. Likely to prey on insects and other small invertebrates in nature.
Known from the Ganges River in northern India , including its floodplain and delta in Bangladesh , plus the Brahmaputra system in the states of Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, and…
notes: Fares best in a well-planted, shady set-up with plenty of surface cover in the form of tall stem or floating plants.
Driftwood can also be used and other plants such as Microsorum or Taxiphyllum spp.

fi-trichogaster-labiosa.title: Thick-lipped Gourami
fi-trichogaster-labiosa.summary: The thick-lipped gourami, Trichogaster labiosa, is a labyrinth fish known only from southern Myanmar, found in shady, weedy rivers and ponds. Easy to keep and peaceful, it is one of the best gouramis…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
notes: Ideally, keep it in a well-planted tank with a dark substrate.
It's a shy, slow-moving species and will not do well without cover into which it can retreat.

fi-helostoma-temminckii.title: Kissing Gourami
fi-helostoma-temminckii.summary: The kissing gourami, Helostoma temminkii, is an anabantoid from southern Indochina and the Malay Archipelago, and the sole member of its family. The widely traded pinkish-white form is a leucistic…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group

Herbivore / algae browser. This species is a highly-specialised, microphagous filter-feeder and possesses very fine gill rakers as well as modified structures on the gill arches to aid in this process.
Described from the island of Java, Indonesia but currently accepted to occur throughout much of southern Indochina and the Malay Archipelago including Vietnam ( Dong Nai river…
notes: Choice of décor is not as critical as water quality and the amount of open swimming-space provided, though it isn't a recommended addition to carefully arranged aquascapes due to its eventual size and tendency to pick at plant leaves.

The addition of some solid surfaces from which the fish can graze biofilm is suggested, with driftwood roots and branches particularly suitable since rocks generally aren't a feature of its natural habitat.
